subject: Intermittent uploads failing over private link — egress NAT/MTU/SG triage
messages:
From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@polestar.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: network_ops@polestar.com, Bob Liao <bob.liao@polestar.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: [Polestar] Intermittent S3 uploads failing over private link — traces attached

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing ~2-5% of customer uploads to our S3 gateway fail intermittently when routed over the Redwood private link from our us-west-2 onprem region. Problems started Friday evening and have increased during high concurrency tests. Symptoms: repeated TCP retransmits then connection resets, and a subset of flows show many zero-window or duplicate-ACKs.

Attached are a short pcap (polestar-pcap-20271201.pcap) and a topology diagram that shows our GRE tunnel to Redwood and the private VPC handoff. We also captured a tcpdump on our egress gateway (tcpdump-logs-20271201.txt).

What we see so far:
- Failures correlate with large PUTs (~1-5 MB) happening concurrently (hundreds of clients).
- Traces indicate out-of-order fragments and MSS-related retransmits.
- We suspect either an MTU/PMTUD issue across the GRE/VPN path or something on your SNAT layer exhausting ephemeral ports / reusing mappings.

Can Redwood confirm whether the SNAT pool on the private handoff is being exhausted or if there are known MTU/GRE fragmentation issues? We'll keep the captures available.

We can be on a call if that's helpful.

Thanks,
Alice Huang
Network Engineering
Polestar Systems

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 08:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Polestar] Intermittent S3 uploads failing over private link — traces attached

Hi Alice — thanks for the captures and the diagram, that's helpful. Apologies for the disruption. I'm escalating to our private-connectivity team and copying the on-call infra folks.

Initial asks from our side to speed triage:
1) Can you confirm whether your VPN/edge is performing MSS clamp on the GRE tunnel? If not, please note the MTU configured on the GRE interface.
2) Can you provide conntrack/snat counters from your egress gateway (show conntrack stats / netstat -nat | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l)?
3) Please keep the pcap timeline — we'll correlate with our NAT logs.

We will:
- Check SNAT pool utilization on the Redwood private handoff for your account.
- Validate whether our upstream firewall is dropping ICMP (PMTUD failures will look like this).
- Look for port reuse and mapping churn under concurrency.

I propose we get a quick bridge at 10:30 PT if that works for you.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alice Huang <alice.huang@polestar.com>, network_ops@polestar.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Polestar] Intermittent S3 uploads failing over private link — traces attached

Naomi / team — I'm taking first-pass on the SNAT side. Quick findings from our edge telemetry for Polestar's private tenancy:
- SNAT pool exhaustion events (short spikes) coincident with the upload peaks. We see ephemeral port churn and some mappings in CLOSE_WAIT longer than expected.
- Current SNAT pool allocation for the tenancy is 4096 ports on the primary egress router. With ~400 concurrent heavy PUTs, we get port pressure and higher probability of mapping collisions (port shadowing).

Preliminary remediation steps I recommend:
1) Increase SNAT pool for Polestar to 16384 ports on the egress node (hot patch, non-disruptive to connection state).
2) Align Polestar ephemeral port range to match the SNAT window (recommend 32768-61000).
3) As a short-term mitigation, add MSS clamp 1420 on the tunnel endpoint to avoid fragmentation over GRE+outer headers. Command (example):
   iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu

I'm attaching a small extract of conntrack logs that shows rapid port reuse.

I'll queue the SNAT pool increase now and will confirm once applied. We still need to validate packet-level path MTU afterwards.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Private Connectivity Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alice Huang <alice.huang@polestar.com>, network_ops@polestar.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Polestar] Intermittent S3 uploads failing over private link — traces attached

Folks — I dug into the forwarding plane traces and BGP next-hops for the time windows in your pcap. Notes:
- We observed asymmetric return paths for ~30% of the affected flows: the client->Polestar->Redwood path is via the GRE tunnel, but some responses are being sent back through a different Internet egress (our upstream peering) due to policy fallback when the GRE became transiently overloaded. That asymmetry worsens PMTUD (ICMP replies get lost).
- Our tunnel endpoints currently do not perform MSS clamping by default, and we've seen ICMP type 3 (fragmentation needed) being dropped by a firewall in the middle of the GRE path (likely at an upstream provider).

Proposed coordinated fixes (order matters):
A) Open ICMP Frag Needed (Type 3, Code 4) across the GRE path so PMTUD can converge — request Polestar to verify their edge is not filtering it.
B) Apply MSS clamp at the GRE/tunnel endpoints (we can push this on our side and request the same on Polestar end).
C) Increase SNAT pool to Marissa's numbers (16384) and expand ephemeral port range alignment to 32768-61000 on their gateways.
D) Add temporary connection draining / rate-limiter on the tunnel to avoid overwhelming a single egress node while SNAT pool resize propagates.

I can schedule a short maintenance window to push the MSS clamp + SNAT increase; need Polestar signoff for the ICMP rule change. Also recommend we run an end-to-end pmtud test and a synthetic high-concurrency PUT test post-change.

Karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Coordination: proposed maintenance window to remediate egress failures (Polestar private tenancy)

Hi Polestar network_ops — thanks for the quick data. To summarize the plan and impact:

What we'll do (Redwood actions) — non-disruptive where possible:
- Increase SNAT pool for your tenancy from 4k -> 16k ports on the primary egress node (applied live; existing sessions preserved).
- Push MSS-clamp on our GRE/tunnel endpoints (iptables mangle TCPMSS clamp to PMTU).
- Enable soft rate-limiting for new flows to avoid transient overload during change propagation.

What we ask Polestar to do (recommended, required for full remediation):
- Confirm you can open ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) across your outbound path to Redwood (this allows PMTUD to converge).
- Align ephemeral port range to 32768-61000 on your egress gateways.

Proposed maintenance window: Fri, Dec 3, 2027 01:00 - 02:00 PT (low traffic window). Rollback plan: revert SNAT pool size and remove MSS clamp if we see regression within the first 15 minutes. We'll run the synthetic PUT test immediately after changes and share results.

Please reply with approval (or an alternative window).

Naomi Feldman
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
